headline: This law lets the Library of Congress buy, maintain, and replace playback equipment for books for blind and physically disabled readers in any format, not just sound recordings.
what_it_does: The law allows the Library of Congress to buy, keep in good repair, and replace devices that play back books for people who are blind or have physical disabilities. Before this law, that authority covered only devices for sound recordings. The law expands it to books in raised characters, sound recordings, or any other format.

who_it_affects.group: Blind people and other physically disabled U.S. residents who use the Library of Congress's National Library Service for the Blind and Physically Handicapped
who_it_affects.how: The Library can now supply and maintain playback equipment for more kinds of books, not only sound recordings.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on July 29, 2016.
